label: EdgePoint R6
description: EdgePoint R6 (EP-R6) - 5x 1G RJ45 + 1x 1G SFP. All five copper ports source 24V/0.7A 2-pair passive PoE (16.8 W each); eth0 also accepts 24V/1.4A passive PoE in. 7 W max excluding PoE output; 65 W PoE envelope on the 24 V / 3 A DC input. Passive PoE only - no 802.3af/at negotiation.

poe.note: DERIVED ENVELOPE, not a quoted budget - Ubiquiti prints no "PoE budget" row for this box on either surface. "Power method (1) DC terminal block, 24V DC, 3A input" = 72 W, less "Max. power consumption 7W (Excludes PoE output)" = 65 W available to the five PSE ports; that ceiling is real, since 5 x 16.8 = 84 W of port capacity exceeds it. Same arithmetic shape as devices/ubiquiti/ep-s16.json, devices/ubiquiti/ep-r8.json and devices/ubiquiti/uisp-r.json. A box fed instead by its 24V/1.4A passive PoE input has 33.6 W of input and therefore at most 33.6 - 7 = 26.6 W for its own PSE ports; a lab that powers it that way states its own figure. Read 2026-11-19: https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp; page 6 "Hardware Specifications EP-R6") and https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/ep-r6 (HTTP 200, 577,753 B, rendered spec table). NOT 802.3: "Passive PoE output (5) 24V / 0.7A, 2-Pair (+4, 5; -7, 8) Passive PoE" carries no detection, and the vendor warns "Do NOT configure eth0 in PoE output mode if you are using a PoE input power source".

notes:
Census, all from the vendor datasheet text layer (https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf - 200, application/pdf, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp, "Models: EP-R6, EP-R8, EP-S16", page 6 = EP-R6 table, read 2026-11-19) unless stated; the rendered techspecs table at https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/ep-r6 prints the same rows.

PORTS - page 6: "Data Ports (5) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Ports, (1) 1 Gbps SFP Port". The LED row names the cage "eth5/SFP", so the copper positions are eth0-eth4 and the cage is the sixth link - what this spec has. No serial console port is printed for the R6, unlike the R8 and S16.

PoE OUTPUT - page 6: "Passive PoE Output (5) 24V / 0.7A, 2-Pair (+4, 5; -7, 8) Passive PoE, eth0 to eth4" - every copper port is a PSE at 16.8 W, and all five are passive 24 V with no 802.3 detection.

PoE INPUT - page 6: "Passive PoE Input (1) 24V / 1.4A, 4-Pair (+1, 2, 4, 5; -3, 6, 7, 8) Passive PoE, eth0", with "Do NOT Configure eth0 in PoE Output Mode if You Are Using a PoE Input Power Source". eth0 therefore carries both `poeIn: 7` (the vendor's "Max. power consumption 7W (Excludes PoE output)" is what it draws) and `poeOut: 16.8`.

WHAT WAS WRONG - the row claimed `poe-pse` and printed no PSE port at all: all five copper ports were dry, so a 24 V airMAX radio had nothing to plug into on the router whose datasheet names it. There was also no `poe` block, so even if a port had been declared `engine/simulator.js` would have skipped the box at `if (!dev.poeBudget) continue;` (parsePoeBudget finds no number in "EP-R6"). The `speedCaps` rung was missing 10M on a 10/100/1000 port.

NOT MODELLED - no 802.3af/at/bt capability (the datasheet prints none), and the 16.8 W per-port figure is the vendor's 24 V x 0.7 A row, not a negotiated class.
